properties.statement:
MEASURED FIRST-HAND IN reflow2's OWN REPO, 2026-08-19 — corroborating ophyd's friction #2 ("evolving a long decision means resending all of it"), and the first report of it with numbers attached.

⚠️ CORRECTED 2026-08-19, SAME DAY, AND THE CORRECTION IS THE USEFUL PART. The first version of this fact claimed `resolve_decision` "removes both failure modes at once". IT DOES NOT, and the error was the ordinary one of filing two things together because they happened in the same session. Anthony asked the claim to be walked through, which is what caught it.

═════════════════════════════════════════════
FAILURE 1 — THE RESEND. This is what `resolve_decision` fixes.

TWO full-property resends of ONE node (`dec:idea-two-more-projects-...`), each to change ONE SENTENCE:
  · 6,242 characters — two Artifact ids became two file paths, after the artifacts were deleted
  · 6,455 characters — the same sentence back again, after the artifacts were restored and parked
≈ 12,700 characters retyped for two one-sentence edits. No tool patches part of a node: `add_decision` merges at PROPERTY granularity, so the smallest possible edit to one sentence is a full retype of everything around it.

THE EXPOSURE IS STATED BY THE TOOL ITSELF, on every one of them: *"NO SNAPSHOT HOLDS THE STATE IT REPLACED — checked, not assumed. The prior value above is now the only copy in existence, and this reply is the only place it appears."*

VERIFIED RATHER THAN ASSUMED, and this is the part worth keeping: for both resends the intended text was written to a file BEFORE the write and diffed against the stored value after. Byte-identical both times. Without that check a single dropped character anywhere in 6,000+ would have been unrecoverable and silent — and the risk scales with the length of the node, so THE NODES MOST WORTH EDITING ARE THE ONES MOST DANGEROUS TO EDIT.

📌 EVIDENCE FOR A FIX ALREADY PROPOSED BY THE REPORTER, NOT A NEW IDEA: ophyd's `resolve_decision(id, resolution_text, status)`, or any field-level patch, removes this failure. Four projects have now reported the pattern; this is the instance with measurements.

═════════════════════════════════════════════
FAILURE 2 — THE MALFORMED WRITE. `resolve_decision` WOULD NOT HAVE PREVENTED IT.

TWICE in the same session, a Decision was written with a closing tag and the `rationale` ARGUMENT embedded inside the `decision` body. Both calls SUCCEEDED, storing trailing tool-call markup in a prose field and no `rationale` property at all. Caught by reading the reply; nothing else noticed.

🛑 WHY THIS IS NOT EVIDENCE FOR `resolve_decision`: BOTH were FIRST WRITES OF NEW NODES. `resolve_decision` appends a resolution to an EXISTING decision — it was not reachable in either case and would have changed nothing. Filing them together was the mistake.

WHAT THEY ARE EVIDENCE FOR is its own item: `dec:idea-a-prose-field-silently-absorbed-tool-call-markup`.

HONEST BOUND ON THE CORRELATION: both malformations were on parameters over 4,000 characters, and none of roughly thirty short writes the same session malformed. That is suggestive that long free-text arguments are where boundaries get mis-emitted, and it is n=2, observational, and confounded — the long writes are also the ones carrying the most retyped text. It does not support more than "worth watching".
